definitions.explanation: Sesame seeds that have been ground or crushed in a mortar, releasing their oils and aroma. A staple seasoning in Japanese home cooking.

examples.japanese: サラダにすりごまをかける。
examples.english: Sprinkle ground sesame on the salad.

examples.japanese: {胡麻|ごま}{和|あ}えにはすりごまを{使|つか}う。
examples.english: Ground sesame is used for sesame-dressed vegetables.

examples.japanese: すりごまは{風味|ふうみ}が{良|よ}いので、{味噌汁|みそしる}の{仕上|しあ}げにも{合|あ}う。
examples.english: Ground sesame has great flavor, so it also works well as a finishing touch for miso soup.

notes:
Written as すりごま (hiragana) or {擂|す}り{胡麻|ごま} (kanji). Made by grinding {胡麻|ごま} (sesame seeds) in a {擂|す}り{鉢|ばち} (mortar). Pre-ground sesame is also sold in supermarkets.

SESAME FORMS IN JAPANESE COOKING:
- {炒|い}りごま: toasted whole sesame seeds
- すりごま: ground sesame seeds
- {練|ね}りごま: sesame paste (tahini-like)
- ごま{油|あぶら}: sesame oil

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- すりごまをかける: to sprinkle ground sesame
- すりごまを{混|ま}ぜる: to mix in ground sesame
- {胡麻|ごま}{和|あ}え: sesame-dressed vegetables (made with ground sesame)
- すりごまで{和|あ}える: to dress with ground sesame

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {炒|い}りごま: toasted sesame — whole seeds that have been dry-roasted; crunchy texture
- {練|ね}りごま: sesame paste — ground further into a smooth paste; used in sauces and dressings
- ごま: sesame — the general term for sesame seeds
